summary: Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. H. F. Hamilton was an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford from around 1877 to 1881. In 1879, he served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service.

J. J. Johnson was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and Durham University. He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from around 1879 to 1913.

J. L. Shaw was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Bimal Krishna Matilal and earned his PhD from Rice University. He founded the Society for Philosophy and Culture and served on the faculty at Victoria University of Wellington (1970–2015).
Philosopher J. M. E. McTaggart studied at Clifton College from around 1882 to 1885. He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1923, where he taught Surendranath Dasgupta.

Indologist and religious studies scholar J. N. Farquhar studied at the University of Aberdeen, Christ Church, Oxford, and under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He later served as Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Manchester (1927–1929).

Indologist and linguist J. N. Reuter studied at Helsinki, Jena, and Berlin under Berthold Delbrück, Albrecht Weber, and Otto Donner. He succeeded Donner in 1905 and served as acting professor at the University of Helsinki from 1891 to 1931.

J. Nelson Fraser worked in Indology and other fields. He served as Professor of English Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1896–1904) and as Principal of the Secondary Training College, Bombay (~1904–1918).

id: P:J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong
summary: J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1904 to 1913. He later held posts at Leiden University in 1922 and from 1935 to 1956.

J. P. Mallory is a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Occidental College and UCLA, he was Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011), later completing degrees and postdoctoral posts in the US.
Indologist J. P. Mills studied at Windlesham House School, Winchester College, and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He later served as a reader at SOAS University of London from 1948 to 1955.
J. Peter L. Gwynn was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at St Columba's College, Trinity College, Hartford (~1935–1938), and University College London (~1938–1939).

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and learned under A. N. Whitehead and A. W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. S. Negi worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi, conducted research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977), and served as chief editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1993–2001).
Indologist J. S. Pade served as a research officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

Japanologist J. Thomas Rimer studied at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held academic posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1985–1993), the University of Pittsburgh (~1993–2012), and UCLA.
Linguist J.-M. Grandjean studied at the University of Lyon under Paul Regnaud.

Linguist and Indologist Jaan Puhvel studied at McGill, Harvard, and Uppsala under Joshua Whatmough, Georges Dumézil, and Stig Wikander. He also studied at and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.

Jabez Cornelius Whitley was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Queens' College (1855–1859). In 1862, he served as a missionary for the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts.

Jack Goody was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1954), and later held a post as a retired professor at the University of Cambridge (~1984–2015).
